forces.title: Shrinking customer base in luxury goods sector
forces.description: The luxury industry is experiencing a shrinking customer base, which poses a significant challenge for companies in the sector. This contraction adds pressure on luxury brands, making the need for innovative strategies to attract and retain customers even more critical. The trend is mentioned in the context of risks and opportunities presented by AI, indicating a broader market shift.
forces.source_title: Winning Over the Customer in the Age of AI: A New Horizon for Luxury

forces.title: Generative AI reshapes luxury brand discoverability
forces.description: Generative Engine Optimization (GEO) is fundamentally altering how luxury brands are discovered, cited, and described in AI-generated search answers. This shift means that consumers are increasingly relying on LLM suggestions for brand discovery, with about 70% of luxury queries not mentioning a specific brand name. Luxury companies must adapt their strategies beyond traditional SEO to ensure visibility and narrative control in this evolving digital landscape.
forces.source_title: Winning Over the Customer in the Age of AI: A New Horizon for Luxury

forces.title: Low AI search and GEO tracking by luxury Maisons
forces.description: A significant proportion of luxury groups and Maisons (52% moderate, 29% weak) report low performance or inconsistent tracking of their AI search and Generative Engine Optimization (GEO) performance. This lack of strategic focus on AI-driven discoverability, despite 75% of luxury prompts expressing discovery or comparison intent, poses a substantial risk of losing potential customers and brand influence in critical stages of the consumer journey. This underinvestment could allow competitors to gain an advantage.
forces.source_title: Winning Over the Customer in the Age of AI: A New Horizon for Luxury

forces.title: External sites dominate luxury brand citations in LLMs
forces.description: In unbranded LLM prompts related to luxury, third-party web content captures the vast majority of citations. Specifically, official brand domains account for only 10% of cited sources for watch queries and 45% for jewelry. This indicates that luxury brands are losing control over their digital narrative to external platforms and content, a critical risk given that third-party content is often overlooked by luxury players in their content strategies.
forces.source_title: Winning Over the Customer in the Age of AI: A New Horizon for Luxury

forces.title: Smaller luxury Maisons can outperform in AI search visibility
forces.description: Generative engines reward relevance and consistency over sheer scale, creating an opportunity for midsize and small luxury Maisons to over-index in AI search visibility. Among the 30 most visible luxury brands on LLMs, many midsize and small Maisons outperformed their market weight in visibility by three to eight times, while larger corporations often captured a visibility share below their revenue share. This allows agile, niche brands to gain significant discoverability.
forces.source_title: Winning Over the Customer in the Age of AI: A New Horizon for Luxury

forces.title: Slow adoption of AI-augmented sales assistance in luxury
forces.description: Despite being viewed as an obvious move and the most advanced customer-facing innovation, widespread adoption of AI-augmented sales assistance is still developing in the luxury sector. Only about 35% of Maisons have deployed solutions with at least some impact, while 45% have no plans or are still evaluating the opportunity. This slow uptake risks hindering improved productivity, personalized service, and elevated customer interactions in the sales process.
forces.source_title: Winning Over the Customer in the Age of AI: A New Horizon for Luxury

forces.title: Luxury industry lags in AI digital personalization deployment
forces.description: AI digital personalization is a recognized opportunity to enhance online customer interactions in luxury, with multi-brand groups actively pushing these capabilities. However, Maisons are significantly lagging, with only 25% currently testing solutions, 15% deploying them, and a mere 5% achieving large-scale deployment with measurable business impact. This slow adoption prevents luxury brands from leveraging AI to create tailored online experiences and strengthen customer relationships effectively.
forces.source_title: Winning Over the Customer in the Age of AI: A New Horizon for Luxury

forces.title: Rising consumer borrowing increases luxury demand sensitivity to credit
forces.description: Consumer spending, especially among middle and lower-income households, is increasingly supported by borrowing, rather than income or savings. This shift means that demand for luxury goods will become more sensitive to tightening credit conditions, rising interest rates, and household debt-service pressures. Luxury businesses need to stress-test demand against these financial factors, as consumers with fewer financial buffers are more exposed to economic shocks, potentially reducing discretionary luxury purchases.
forces.source_title: Consumer Spending in Canada Is Shifting, Just Not How You’d Expect

forces.title: Illiquid wealth and inflation limit discretionary luxury spending
forces.description: Despite asset gains supporting consumer confidence, much of this wealth is tied up in illiquid assets like homes, making it difficult to access for discretionary luxury purchases. Furthermore, if higher oil prices lead to broader inflation, consumers may struggle to maintain their purchasing power. This combination increases the need for financing, trade-in, or deferred-payment options for luxury goods, creating a headwind for spontaneous high-ticket purchases, particularly for financially constrained consumers.
forces.source_title: Consumer Spending in Canada Is Shifting, Just Not How You’d Expect

viewpoints.title: Luxury goods demand sensitive to credit as consumer spending relies on borrowing
viewpoints.description: BCG analysis indicates that for luxury goods, demand is becoming more sensitive to interest rates, credit availability, and household debt-service pressure. This is due to a growing proportion of consumer spending being supported by borrowing, rather than income growth or savings, particularly among middle and lower-income households. While the data is from Canada, the report by BCG Global implies these insights are relevant for businesses operating in K-shaped economies, which could include parts of Europe. This trend poses a significant challenge for luxury companies dependent on discretionary spending.
viewpoints.source_title: Consumer Spending in Canada Is Shifting, Just Not How You’d Expect

viewpoints.title: Luxury industry's slow AI adoption contrasts with rapid consumer embrace
viewpoints.description: Bain highlights a critical disconnect where the luxury industry remains cautious regarding AI adoption, despite its clients rapidly embracing generative AI tools. Consumers are remapping their luxury purchase journeys, increasingly using Large Language Models (LLMs) as digital concierges to discover brands and shape decisions. This wariness within the industry risks ceding narrative control and losing potential customers, especially given the sector's already shrinking customer base. Adapting to AI-driven discoverability and enhancing client experiences is crucial for future growth.
viewpoints.source_title: Winning Over the Customer in the Age of AI: A New Horizon for Luxury

viewpoints.title: AI presents dual risks and opportunities for luxury sector amidst customer base shrinkage
viewpoints.description: Bain identifies that while AI offers significant opportunities for luxury companies to build brand awareness, reinvent customer acquisition, reinforce messaging, enrich sales, and elevate client experiences, it also brings substantial risks. The industry faces the danger of losing potential customers and narrative control, a concern amplified by an already shrinking customer base. Effective Generative Engine Optimization (GEO) and customer-facing AI innovations are crucial, yet widespread adoption remains slow, indicating a need for strategic investment and cross-functional coordination to leverage AI's upside potential.
viewpoints.source_title: Winning Over the Customer in the Age of AI: A New Horizon for Luxury
